Create detail tables for the variables
Provide prefix for the output tables:

children.text: This custom step compares a real dataset against a synthetic dataset to produce a composite similarity score. It evaluates data fidelity across four dimensions: numeric univariate similarity (mean, median, standard deviation), categorical univariate similarity (total variation distance and Jensen–Shannon divergence), categorical relationship fidelity (pairwise Cramér's V comparison), and numeric relationship fidelity (pairwise Spearman correlation comparison). Each dimension produces a detail table for drill-through analysis, and the results are combined into weighted statistical and relational similarity scores — proportional to the number of numeric and categorical variables — giving a single overall similarity percentage. An optional filter condition allows evaluation on specific subsets of the data.

1. Real data — the two-level name of the real (original) dataset to use as the baseline for comparison (e.g. CASUSER.REAL).
2. Synthetic data — the two-level name of the synthetic dataset to evaluate against the real data (e.g. CASUSER.SYNTH).
3. Output library — the output library where all five result tables will be written (e.g. WORK or CASUSER). Defaults to WORK. 
4. Summary table — Always written as similarity_scores in the output library (with any prefix applied). The output port lets you connect downstream flow nodes; the Table node itself is where you'd assign a custom flow name if needed.
5. Create detail tables (checkbox) — When ticked, four detail tables are written to the output library alongside the summary (per-variable and per-pair breakdowns for drill-through analysis). When unticked, only the summary table is kept.
6. Table prefix (optional) — Prefix prepended to all output table names (e.g. q4 produces q4_similarity_scores). Useful when running multiple comparisons in the same library without overwriting previous results.
7. Filter Condition — an optional WHERE expression to subset both tables before evaluation (e.g. bad=1). Leave blank to run against the full tables.
The framework is mentioned in a presentation at SAS Innovate 2026 - watch here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0waLptixaOk&list=PLVBcK_IpFVi-BXicJ5ZMcXuPNQTphJuhv&index=146&t=1s
